deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a page of German lecture notes or an excerpt on ancient Greek history: the Greek colonies on Sicily, specifically Syracuse. It continues from folio 67, which covered Magna Graecia and the founding of Syracuse as a Corinthian colony, and runs into folio 69.

Content, in order:

(1) End of the 1st period (founding of Syracuse 735 to Gelon 484). During this period the city founded further colonies, e.g. Camarina. Factions soon arose. In 485 the rich (historically the Gamoroi, the landholding aristocracy) were driven out by the democratic party. The exiles sought protection from Gelon, ruler of Gela. He led them back and made himself master of the city; 'Lande' is struck out and replaced by 'Stadt'.

(2) Heading: '2. Periode. Von Gelon bis auf die Vertreibung Thrasybuls, 484–466' (2nd period, from Gelon to the expulsion of Thrasybulus). Gelon ruled 7 years. He brought many new citizens to Syracuse, enlarged the city, and so gained, as it were, a garrison. He increased his power further through his victory over the Carthaginians (Himera, 480). Previously only a general, he was now proclaimed king by the people (480). At his death his brother Hiero I succeeded; 'Sohn' (son) is struck out and replaced by 'Bruder' (brother). Hiero ruled until 466, kept a splendid court and promoted art and learning. In 466 the third brother, Thrasybulus, followed. He became a great tyrant and was expelled after only 8 months.

(3) Heading: '3. Periode. Von der Vertreibung Thrasybuls bis auf die Erhebung Dionysius I, 466–405' (3rd period, from the expulsion of Thrasybulus to the rise of Dionysius I). The text of this period continues on the next folio.

The right margin shows the cut-off edge of the facing page: Diese…, Allein…, 412…, 410…, Selinus. These match lines of folio 69 and are not marginalia belonging to this page.

There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct. The material is routine textbook ancient history of the kind taught at Göttingen around 1800 (Heeren-style 'Perioden' structure). The neat but unformed hand looks like student notes, and the filing under 'HB.Lagrange1816' looks incidental. Attribution of the hand to Gauss is uncertain.
errors: Small date inconsistency in the source: the text puts Gelon's seizure of Syracuse in 485, but the period heading starts at 484. Modern chronology gives 485 BC for Gelon taking Syracuse. With 'regierte 7 Jahr' this yields 485–478, which is consistent with the standard date.
Hiero I's death is usually dated 467/466 BC and Thrasybulus' expulsion to 466/465. The notes' '466' is acceptable.
'Nach 8 Monaten' for Thrasybulus: Diodorus (XI.66–68) gives a reign of about one year, some modern accounts say 11 months. This is a minor discrepancy in the notes, not a derivation error.
'Der 3te Bruder Thrasybul': there were four Deinomenid brothers (Gelon, Hiero, Polyzalus, Thrasybulus). Thrasybulus was the third to rule Syracuse but the youngest brother, so the phrasing is loose.

results.what: Outline of Syracusan history: factional strife and Gelon's takeover (485), Gelon's reign and victory over Carthage (480), Hiero I to 466, expulsion of Thrasybulus (466), next period to Dionysius I (405)
results.modern_name: Deinomenid tyranny at Syracuse (standard ancient history)
results.usually_credited_to: Herodotus VII and Diodorus Siculus XI as ancient sources; in Göttingen teaching of the period, A. H. L. Heeren and similar compendia

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics. It is routine lecture or excerpt notes on ancient Sicilian history, probably student notes. Even if the hand is Gauss's (he attended history lectures as a student), the content is standard textbook material.

checkable.asserts: Gelon taking power in 485 BC and ruling 7 years ends his reign in 478 BC, the standard date of his death.
The 2nd period as headed (484–466) spans 18 years: Gelon's 7 plus Hiero's roughly 11.

transcription_corrections: Line 6: read 'der sie auch wieder zurückführte und sich selbst der {+Stadt+} [-Lande-] bemächtigte' rather than 'der sie wieder [?] zurück und führte [?] ..'.

Line 'Daher war er auch beliebt geworden, jetzt war [?] da er aber vom Volk zum König ausgerufen' should read approximately 'Vorher war er nur Feldherr gewesen, jetzt ward er aber vom Volke zum König ausgerufen. 480'.
'erwarb [?] gleichsam eine Garnison' is probably 'erwarb sich gleichsam eine Garnison'.
'Er zog [?] viele neue Bürger dahin': 'zog' is correct, and the word 'zog' is overwritten or corrected in the manuscript.
The right-margin fragments (Diese…, Allein…, 412…, 410…, Selinus) belong to the edge of the facing folio 69, not to this page.
